clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Panama features a diverse set of road lines, but the most common combination is solid outer white with an inner yellow line. However, those are not unique to Panama.
Within Latin America, solid outer white lines with no middle line are almost unique to Panama.

clues.title: Stop sign: Alto
text: Panama, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: White Truck
text: Panama features a large white pickup truck which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
There is always a short black antenna attached to the front of the car.
Beware that the antenna can sometimes be blurred.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Small Tree Fences
text: Most roads are paralleled by fences that are partly or fully made out of small trees.
The rest of the fence posts are also almost always wooden.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture
text: Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing.
The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof.
Many windows have bars on them for security.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: Big Font ALTO
text: Panama uses the Spanish word “ALTO” on stop signs.
Mexico and Guatemala also use “ALTO”, but the font is thinner.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top.
Rarely, the strip can have other colours.
Front plates are not required in Panama.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Aguadulce Fields
text: The region around Aguadulce is relatively flat and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very brown or orange soil.

clues.title: Landscape: David Fields
text: The area around David is very flat, with lots of fairly open fields. Usually, mountains will be visible to the north and northeast.

clues.title: Landscape: Tropical Rainforest
text: Green tropical landscapes with palm trees and very tall grass are common around Colón and Panama City.

clues.title: Landscape: Volcán Landscape
text: A mountainous landscape with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.

clues.title: Panama
text: The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama.
The numbers with a smaller font indicate potentially useful regional two-digit codes.
NOTE: Only phone numbers with 7 digits are helpful, and any numbers starting with 5, 6, or 8 are useless as well.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: horizontal marker
text: East of Panama City and around Colon, utility pole marker are white or yellow and vertical.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: round concrete
text: Panama uses a wide variety of poles, but the most common type is a round concrete pole.
NOTE: Kenya has most of the time wooden poles with metallic support while Panama typically use wooden support.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: thin vertical marker
text: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border are most common in the Colón Province.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: vertical marker
text: The eastern provinces often have tall vertical plates that can be yellow or white. They are commonly attached to poles by black zip ties.
NOTE: Be careful there are white vertical plates, often attached by metallic zip ties. They are slightly wider than the eastern plates and always have 6 digits.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
